headline: High-risk shared-webapp pair: open-webui can ingest and act on Chatwoot data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP/OpenAPI tool surfaces and browser/subprocess execution, while chatwoot handles customer messages and supports integrations that can carry attacker-controlled content. If Chatwoot content is fed into open-webui, raw text can become instructions. The interaction is plausible from docs alone, but not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Chatwoot messages are forwarded into Open WebUI prompts or MCP tools without sanitization
IF Open WebUI parses Chatwoot-exported content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any Chatwoot-to-Open WebUI content bridge
Strip role-like tokens and tool directives before forwarding text
Use a read-only export format for shared content
Add provenance labels to all imported Chatwoot messages
requires-engineering: enforce prompt-injection filtering at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages; open-webui handles files, persistent memory, and API keys and can send data to broad network egress targets. A shared workspace or imported conversation can leak sensitive customer data into Open WebUI storage or third-party APIs. The pairwise path is documented only indirectly, so I choose the higher severity under uncertainty.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or exports are loaded into Open WebUI
IF Open WebUI syncs imported content to external APIs or persistent memory
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Open WebUI
Turn off external API connectors for sensitive sessions
Use a separate workspace for customer data
Purge Open WebUI persistent memory after any import
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on imported files and messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: chatwoot is a customer-support system with integrations, while open-webui can run browsers, subprocesses, and use persistent shared sessions. If both write to the same files, tickets, or shared artifacts, they can overwrite each other or race on mutable state. The profiles show overlapping write-adjacent surfaces, but not a proven same-directory lock failure, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted directory or shared artifact store
IF Chatwoot integrations and Open WebUI tools modify the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Make shared resources read-only for one side
Disable concurrent writes to the same ticket or file
Check for duplicate updates before saving
requires-engineering: add resource locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act through tools, browsers, and subprocesses, and chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports. If Open WebUI consumes Chatwoot output as authoritative, it can propagate errors into downstream actions or responses. Because the pair lacks a documented verification boundary, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Open WebUI uses Chatwoot-generated text as a source of truth
IF Open WebUI triggers tool actions or drafts responses from unverified Chatwoot output
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on Chatwoot output
Mark Chatwoot content as untrusted input in Open WebUI
Add a verification step before sending messages or executing tools
Limit Open WebUI to summarization only for Chatwoot data
requires-engineering: implement source-citation and validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: chatwoot processes customer data, contact profiles, and interaction history, while open-webui handles files, persistent memory, usage analytics, and API keys with broad network egress. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if customer records are imported into Open WebUI. No direct residency or certification evidence is provided, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is stored in Open WebUI persistent memory or analytics
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Avoid storing customer data in Open WebUI memory
Set short retention on imported artifacts
Document which system is the system of record
Delete imported customer data after use
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
